verses.original: Πόθεν πόλεμοι καὶ πόθεν μάχαι ἐν ὑμῖν οὐκ ἐντεῦθεν ἐκ τῶν ἡδονῶν ὑμῶν τῶν στρατευομένων ἐν τοῖς μέλεσιν ὑμῶν
verses.transliteration: Pothen polemoi kai pothen machai en hymin ouk enteuthen ek tōn hēdonōn hymōn tōn strateuomenōn en tois melesin hymōn
verses.literal: What causes conflicts and quarrels among you Don’t they come from the passions at war within you . . . . . .
verses.literalPt: Donde vêm as guerras, e donde vêm as contendas entre vós? Não vêm, porventura, disto: dos vossos deleites, que combatem nos vossos membros?

verses.original: ἐπιθυμεῖτε καὶ οὐκ ἔχετε φονεύετε καὶ ζηλοῦτε καὶ οὐ δύνασθε ἐπιτυχεῖν μάχεσθε καὶ πολεμεῖτε οὐκ ἔχετε διὰ τὸ μὴ αἰτεῖσθαι ὑμᾶς
verses.transliteration: epithymeite kai ouk echete phoneuete kai zēloute kai ou dynasthe epitychein machesthe kai polemeite ouk echete dia to mē aiteisthai hymas
verses.literal: You crave what you do not have you kill and covet but are unable to obtain it You quarrel and fight You do not have because you do not ask
verses.literalPt: Cobiçais e não possuis; matais, e invejais, e não podeis alcançar; contendeis e fazeis guerras. Não tendes, porque não pedis;

verses.original: αἰτεῖτε καὶ οὐ λαμβάνετε διότι κακῶς αἰτεῖσθε ἵνα ἐν ταῖς ἡδοναῖς ὑμῶν δαπανήσητε
verses.transliteration: aiteite kai ou lambanete dioti kakōs aiteisthe hina en tais hēdonais hymōn dapanēsēte
verses.literal: And when you do ask . . . you do not receive because you ask with wrong motives that you may squander it on your pleasures
verses.literalPt: pedis e não recebeis, porque pedis erradamente, a fim de o despenderdes em vossos deleites.

verses.original: Μοιχαλίδες οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι ἡ φιλία τοῦ κόσμου ἔχθρα τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐστιν ὃς ἐὰν οὖν βουληθῇ φίλος εἶναι τοῦ κόσμου ἐχθρὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ καθίσταται
verses.transliteration: Moichalides ouk oidate hoti hē philia tou kosmou echthra tou Theou estin hos ean oun boulēthē philos einai tou kosmou echthros tou Theou kathistatai
verses.literal: You adulteresses Do you not know that friendship with the world is hostility toward God Therefore whoever . . . chooses to be a friend of the world renders himself an enemy of God
verses.literalPt: Adúlteros, não sabeis que a amizade do mundo é inimizade contra Deus? Aquele, pois, que quiser ser amigo do mundo constitui-se inimigo de Deus.

verses.original: ἢ δοκεῖτε ὅτι κενῶς ἡ γραφὴ λέγει Πρὸς φθόνον ἐπιποθεῖ τὸ πνεῦμα ὃ κατῴκισεν ἐν ἡμῖν
verses.transliteration: ē dokeite hoti kenōs hē graphē legei Pros phthonon epipothei to pneuma ho katōkisen en hēmin
verses.literal: Or do you think the Scripture says without reason that the Spirit He caused to dwell in us yearns with envy
verses.literalPt: Acaso, julgais que é em vão que a Escritura diz: Com zelos anela por nós o Espírito, que ele fez habitar em nós?

verses.original: μείζονα δὲ δίδωσιν χάριν διὸ λέγει Ὁ Θεὸς ὑπερηφάνοις ἀντιτάσσεται ταπεινοῖς δὲ δίδωσιν χάριν
verses.transliteration: meizona de didōsin charin dio legei Ho Theos hyperēphanois antitassetai tapeinois de didōsin charin
verses.literal: But He gives us more grace This is why it says God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble
verses.literalPt: Porém dá maior graça, pelo que também diz: Deus resiste aos orgulhosos e dá graça aos humildes.

verses.original: Ὑποτάγητε οὖν τῷ Θεῷ ἀντίστητε δὲ τῷ διαβόλῳ καὶ φεύξεται ἀφ’ ὑμῶν
verses.transliteration: Hypotagēte oun tō Theō antistēte de tō diabolō kai pheuxetai aph’ hymōn
verses.literal: Submit yourselves then to God Resist the devil and he will flee from you
verses.literalPt: Sujeitai-vos, pois, a Deus; mas resisti ao Diabo, e ele fugirá de vós.

verses.original: ἐγγίσατε τῷ Θεῷ καὶ ἐγγιεῖ ὑμῖν καθαρίσατε χεῖρας ἁμαρτωλοί καὶ ἁγνίσατε καρδίας δίψυχοι
verses.transliteration: engisate tō Theō kai engiei hymin katharisate cheiras hamartōloi kai hagnisate kardias dipsychoi
verses.literal: Draw near to God and He will draw near to you Cleanse your hands you sinners and purify your hearts you double-minded
verses.literalPt: Chegai-vos para Deus, e ele se chegará para vós. Lavai, pecadores, as mãos, e, vós de espírito vacilante, purificai os corações.

verses.original: ταλαιπωρήσατε καὶ πενθήσατε καὶ κλαύσατε ὁ γέλως ὑμῶν εἰς πένθος μετατραπήτω καὶ ἡ χαρὰ εἰς κατήφειαν
verses.transliteration: talaipōrēsate kai penthēsate kai klausate ho gelōs hymōn eis penthos metatrapētō kai hē chara eis katēpheian
verses.literal: Grieve mourn and weep Turn your laughter to mourning and your joy to gloom
verses.literalPt: Afligi-vos, pranteai e chorai; converta-se o vosso riso em pranto, e a vossa alegria, em tristeza.

verses.original: ταπεινώθητε ἐνώπιον Κυρίου καὶ ὑψώσει ὑμᾶς
verses.transliteration: tapeinōthēte enōpion Kyriou kai hypsōsei hymas
verses.literal: Humble yourselves before the Lord and He will exalt you
verses.literalPt: Humilhai-vos diante do Senhor, e ele vos exaltará.

verses.original: Μὴ καταλαλεῖτε ἀλλήλων ἀδελφοί ὁ καταλαλῶν ἀδελφοῦ ἢ κρίνων τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ καταλαλεῖ νόμου καὶ κρίνει νόμον εἰ δὲ νόμον κρίνεις οὐκ εἶ ποιητὴς νόμου ἀλλὰ κριτής
verses.transliteration: Mē katalaleite allēlōn adelphoi ho katalalōn adelphou ē krinōn ton adelphon autou katalalei nomou kai krinei nomon ei de nomon krineis ouk ei poiētēs nomou alla kritēs
verses.literal: Brothers do not slander one another Anyone who speaks against his brother or judges him speaks against the law and judges it And if you judge the law you are not a practitioner of the law but a judge of it
verses.literalPt: Irmãos, não faleis mal uns dos outros. Aquele que fala mal dum irmão ou julga a seu irmão fala contra a Lei e julga a Lei; mas, se julgas a Lei, não és mais observador da Lei, mas juiz.

verses.original: εἷς ἐστιν ὁ νομοθέτης καὶ κριτής ὁ δυνάμενος σῶσαι καὶ ἀπολέσαι σὺ δὲ τίς εἶ ὁ κρίνων τὸν πλησίον
verses.transliteration: heis estin ho nomothetēs kai kritēs ho dynamenos sōsai kai apolesai sy de tis ei ho krinōn ton plēsion
verses.literal: There is only one Lawgiver and Judge the One who is able to save and destroy But who are you to judge your neighbor
verses.literalPt: Um só é o Legislador e o Juiz, aquele que pode salvar e destruir; tu, porém, quem és que julgas ao teu próximo?

verses.original: Ἄγε νῦν οἱ λέγοντες Σήμερον ἢ αὔριον πορευσόμεθα εἰς τήνδε τὴν πόλιν καὶ ποιήσομεν ἐκεῖ ἐνιαυτὸν καὶ ἐμπορευσόμεθα καὶ κερδήσομεν
verses.transliteration: Age nyn hoi legontes Sēmeron ē aurion poreusometha eis tēnde tēn polin kai poiēsomen ekei eniauton kai emporeusometha kai kerdēsomen
verses.literal: Come now you who say Today or tomorrow we will go to this or that city spend a year there carry on business and make a profit
verses.literalPt: Eia agora, vós que dizeis: Hoje ou amanhã, iremos a tal cidade, ali passaremos um ano, negociaremos e ganharemos.

verses.original: οἵτινες οὐκ ἐπίστασθε τὸ τῆς αὔριον ποία ἡ ζωὴ ὑμῶν ἀτμὶς γάρ ἐστε ἡ πρὸς ὀλίγον φαινομένη ἔπειτα καὶ ἀφανιζομένη
verses.transliteration: hoitines ouk epistasthe to tēs aurion poia hē zōē hymōn atmis gar este hē pros oligon phainomenē epeita kai aphanizomenē
verses.literal: You do not even know . . . what will happen tomorrow What is your life You are a mist that appears for a little while and then vanishes
verses.literalPt: Vós não sabeis o que sucederá amanhã. Que é a vossa vida? Pois nada mais sois que um vapor que aparece por um pouco e logo se desvanece.

verses.original: Ἀντὶ τοῦ λέγειν ὑμᾶς Ἐὰν ὁ Κύριος θελήσῃ καὶ ζήσομεν καὶ ποιήσομεν τοῦτο ἢ ἐκεῖνο
verses.transliteration: Anti tou legein hymas Ean ho Kyrios thelēsē kai zēsomen kai poiēsomen touto ē ekeino
verses.literal: Instead you ought to say If the Lord is willing we will live and do this or that
verses.literalPt: Em vez de dizerdes: Se o Senhor quiser, viveremos e faremos isto ou aquilo.

verses.original: νῦν δὲ καυχᾶσθε ἐν ταῖς ἀλαζονείαις ὑμῶν πᾶσα καύχησις τοιαύτη πονηρά ἐστιν
verses.transliteration: nyn de kauchasthe en tais alazoneiais hymōn pasa kauchēsis toiautē ponēra estin
verses.literal: As it is you boast in your proud intentions All such boasting is evil
verses.literalPt: Agora, porém, vos jactais das vossas presunções. Toda jactância tal como esta é maligna.

verses.original: εἰδότι οὖν καλὸν ποιεῖν καὶ μὴ ποιοῦντι ἁμαρτία αὐτῷ ἐστιν
verses.transliteration: eidoti oun kalon poiein kai mē poiounti hamartia autō estin
verses.literal: Anyone then who knows the right thing to do yet fails to do it is guilty of sin
verses.literalPt: Portanto, para quem sabe fazer o bem e não o faz, para este é pecado.
